_comment_security: Channel permissions, verified empirically against Centrifugo v5.4.9 by
api/tests/test_centrifugo.py — do not relax these without re-running it.
allow_subscribe_for_client: false (the DEFAULT, stated here explicitly)
A client cannot subscribe to room:* or user:* on its own. It must
present a subscription token minted by PAL, and PAL only mints one
after services.chat.authz.is_room_member() passes. This is what
preserves the RBAC/PHI guarantees after the migration off /ws/chat.
Clients may never publish directly. Messages go REST -> FastAPI
(persist + authorize + PHI-redact) -> server API publish. A client
cannot inject an unpersisted or unredacted frame into a family hub.
Replaces the Redis room_members:* set the native manager kept.
Replace token_hmac_secret_key and api_key with real secrets. They must
match CENTRIFUGO_TOKEN_HMAC_SECRET and CENTRIFUGO_API_KEY in api/.env.
_comment_scale: 1. Run several Centrifugo nodes behind a WS-capable load balancer and
set an engine so they form one cluster:
(or the Redis Cluster / Sentinel variants). Sticky sessions are NOT
required — any node can serve any user.
2. Raise file-descriptor limits: ulimit -n 1000000 per node.
3. PAL's API pods stay stateless; they only make short HTTP calls to
/api/publish, so the FastAPI DB pool is no longer coupled to the
number of open sockets. That coupling was the real ceiling before.
